title: McDonald's Plans $8.5 Billion Restaurant Overhaul
paragraphs: McDonald's has announced an $8.5 billion plan to modernize its restaurants around the world, as the fast-food giant seeks to attract more customers and make its stores more efficient.

The company revealed the plan on September 23 at a meeting with investors in Chicago. The money will be provided to support franchisees, the independent business owners who run most McDonald's restaurants, through 2036, with about $5 billion of it coming by 2030. The support will include help with building costs as well as rent relief. The investments will be introduced gradually, as different markets and individual franchisees become ready.

Customers can expect to see a number of changes. Remodeled restaurants will include lockers for delivery orders, coffee preparation areas that are easier to see, bigger play areas and improved kitchen layouts. McDonald's is also introducing ArchIQ, a system developed with Google that uses artificial intelligence to improve order accuracy and automate tasks such as managing stock and scheduling staff. In addition, the company is testing an AI drive-thru ordering system called Archy, which can take orders in English and Spanish with 90% accuracy.
McDonald's said it needs to make these changes because sales in the US and some other markets have been flat. To grow, it must win customers from competitors and make its restaurants more productive.

The plan will also be costly for franchisees. In the US, franchisees typically spend up to $450,000 every ten years on required remodels. Under the new plan, they will need to spend an additional $800,000 over time, although McDonald's will cover part of this cost. The company expects the improvements to add about $100,000 a year in cash flow for the average US restaurant.
Investors were worried about the cost of upgrading the company's 46,000 restaurants worldwide. McDonald's shares fell nearly 5% on the day of the announcement, their biggest drop since April 2025.
Skye Anderson, president of McDonald's USA, said the company needs to keep giving customers more reasons to make McDonald's their first choice.
